clue.text: Supporter trouble is on the rise for City

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football club's backers are increasingly in strife over their City side.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'trouble is' turns over; the supporter stays the right way round in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the purpose-built capital city of Brazil.

clue.text: Angler pulled up unknown fish

indicators.note: pulling something up in a down entry lifts it bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a rod is an angler, as in rod and line fishermen
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A fisherman hauls in a fish he cannot identify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angler' also suggests the anglerfish, but here it is the person with a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The dory, or John Dory, is an edible sea fish.

clue.text: Shower in toilet is hot

blocks.note: lav is short for lavatory
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A bathroom complaint: the shower in the loo runs hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' reads as the bathroom fitting, but it is the verb, to give generously.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish gifts on someone is to shower them with gifts, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Here, the Marseillaise wins award for muppet

indicators.note: a word that wins something takes it in and holds it

blocks.note: ici is French for here, signalled by the Marseillaise
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
le is French for the; the Marseillaise is the French anthem

explanation.surface: Someone singing the French anthem gets a prize for being a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Marseillaise' tells you to work in French: ICI for here, LE for the. Muppet is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Muppet is informal British slang for a stupid person, so an imbecile.

clue.text: Spooner's old woman skewers seafood

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: a crone is an old woman and stabs means skewers; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: An elderly lady spears the seafood with her fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone crabs are edible crabs of the western Atlantic, prized for their claws.

clue.text: Car sounding like FAB 1?

indicators.note: sounding like says the answer is spoken the same as another word

blocks.note: the Beatles were the Fab Four, so one of them is a Beatle

explanation.surface: FAB 1 is Lady Penelope's pink Rolls-Royce in Thunderbirds, so this asks which car resembles it.
explanation.walkthrough: FAB 1 points at Thunderbirds, but the question mark signals one of the Fab Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen Beetle is a famous small car model.

clue.text: Second half of Mozart's organ composition is imperious

indicators.note: only the latter half of the composer's name is kept, the front half thrown away
a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged anew

blocks.note: the composer's name, of which only the back three letters survive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grandiose Mozart work for organ comes across as haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious and arrogant both describe a domineering, haughty manner.

clue.text: Outspoken Bond intoxicated secretary

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a tie is a bond
pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A frank James Bond is drunk and eyeing a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is simply a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist was the classic office secretary role, typing letters.

clue.text: Meghan's opening Spare for old lady

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the name is used

blocks.note: the initial of the name
a spare one is the other one

explanation.surface: Meghan Markle's first sight of Prince Harry's memoir Spare, seen through a mother-in-law's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' evokes Prince Harry's memoir, but it means extra or other.
explanation.definitionFit: Old lady is informal slang for one's mother.

clue.text: Grey area's shrinking

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
shrinking as in timid, shrinking violet

explanation.surface: A grey zone of land is getting smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrinking' looks like getting smaller, but it means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy describes the pale grey colour of ash.

clue.text: Sculpture of T'ang empire is steep

indicators.note: a sculpture is something shaped and remodelled, so the letters are moulded into new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An art historian notes that a Tang dynasty statue is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' is not pricey here but the verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak or saturate it, which is to impregnate it.

clue.text: Jumper cleared ditch in Irish festival

indicators.note: a cleared ditch is emptied of its contents, leaving only its two ends

blocks.note: a flea is a jumping insect
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A horse jumped a ditch cleanly at an Irish country fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a showjumper or a sweater; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleadh is an Irish festival of traditional music and dance.

clue.text: Tackled editor following program on fish

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the editor is sent to the end behind the rest

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
the roach is a freshwater fish
ED is the usual short form of editor

explanation.surface: An editor took on a TV show about fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the editor after the rest; 'on' places the program before the fish in an across-style charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach a problem or task is to tackle it or set about it.

clue.text: Rat Scabies finally backing metal singer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the drummer's surname
backing means going backwards, so the word runs right to left

blocks.note: the final letter
tin is a metal
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: Rat Scabies, drummer of punk band the Damned, ends up supporting a heavy metal vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat Scabies' reads as one name, but Rat is the definition and Scabies gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform, so a rat is a snitcher or informer.

clue.text: Spiteful wife's like a viper?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
the asp is a venomous snake, here loosely a viper
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: A spiteful wife is likened to a venomous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an asp is not strictly a viper.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means irritable and sharply sarcastic, like a wasp's sting.

clue.text: Kent lose badly in sporting event

indicators.note: doing something badly gets it wrong, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Kent, the county cricket team, suffers a heavy defeat in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeleton is a Winter Olympic sliding sport, riding a sled head first.

clue.text: Revolutionary force concerning mardy bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the word is reassembled

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel army discusses the Arctic Monkeys song Mardy Bum.
explanation.walkthrough: Mardy is Northern English for sulky; 'Mardy Bum' is an Arctic Monkeys song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the Soviet military created after the Bolshevik revolution.

clue.text: 22dn edges away from Pulp singer

indicators.note: taking the edges away removes the first and last letters

blocks.note: a midge is an example of the answer to 22 down
a pulp of fruit or veg is a purée

explanation.surface: An insect sidles away from Jarvis Cocker, frontman of the band Pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulp singer' looks like Jarvis Cocker, but Pulp is a mash and the definition is 'singer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Midge Ure is the Scottish frontman of Ultravox and co-organiser of Live Aid.

clue.text: Bar pulled up about adult show

indicators.note: pulled up in a down entry lifts the word so it reads from the bottom
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a lever is a bar
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A pub is shut down over an adult entertainment show.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to reveal or disclose it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: 24ac loos unfortunately out of use

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: the answer to 24 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: Toilets at a beet farm are sadly no longer working.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means no longer used, outdated and discarded.

clue.text: Drinker is only just fine for start of evening

indicators.note: one thing given for another takes its place in the word
'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'evening'

blocks.note: barely means only just
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the first letter

explanation.surface: A pub regular is just about all right as the evening begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The E in the word for only just is swapped out for F.
explanation.definitionFit: A barfly is someone who spends a lot of time drinking in bars.

clue.text: Moaned audibly after hip locked up

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds

blocks.note: in means fashionable, hip
to sigh is to moan

explanation.surface: Someone groaned noisily after a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks like the joint, but it means trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, so locked up.

clue.text: Vet dropping soft animal

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it out of the word

blocks.note: to vet is to inspect
P is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon lets a fluffy pet fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor but is the verb to check.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect is a small invertebrate animal with six legs.

clue.text: Players in cocaine blunder before Queen's

blocks.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
ricket is informal for a mistake
ER, Elizabeth Regina, plus the 's

explanation.surface: Musicians are caught up in a drug scandal ahead of the band Queen's set.
explanation.walkthrough: Ricket is an informal word, chiefly Northern English, for a blunder. ER is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers are the players in a game of cricket.

clue.text: Speculate about the end of Joe Root

indicators.note: the end means only the final letter of the first name is used
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to bet is to speculate or gamble
the last letter

explanation.surface: Gamblers wager on when the England batter Joe Root will be out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joe Root' reads as the England cricketer; Root is the definition, and only Joe supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beet is a root vegetable, as in beetroot.

clue.text: The Two Ronnies initially leaving soup

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word beside it
leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: the first letter
broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: The comedy duo the Two Ronnies walk out of a soup sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Two Ronnies were a classic British TV comedy double act; 'The Two' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both means the two together, a pronoun synonym.

clue.text: This is one party game

blocks.note: the line being read is itself a clue
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone presents a game to play at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is one' refers to the clue itself. 'party game' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is a board game of solving a murder mystery.

clue.text: John pinching Nick's lines in chat room

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so one word is clasped inside another

blocks.note: john is slang for toilet
a nick is a small cut
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: A man called John steals Nick's script for an online forum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' and 'Nick' look like names; they are a toilet and a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A locutory is a room in a monastery set aside for conversation.
